title: Staged endpoint authenticator and DNS priming worker for safer control-plane provisioning
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Add staged endpoint authenticator and DNS priming worker to reduce control-plane cutovers during endpoint rotation. No customer-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers reported transient control-plane failures during endpoint credential rotation and large-scale subnet recompositions: requests would briefly route to newly created endpoints before security groups, route tables, and private DNS records were fully reconcilable. This resulted in brief auth errors and audit log gaps for Private deployments (SUP-9812). Goal: introduce a staged authenticator that performs a non-disruptive pre-provisioning pass and a DNS priming worker that ensures DNS glue and resolver rules are warmed prior to cutover.

What this PR does (summary):
- Implements an endpoint-authenticator controller that validates endpoint IAM/SG bindings against a desired-state plan and exposes a "ready-for-swap" predicate.
- Adds a DNS priming worker that creates and validates temporary CNAME/A records and Route53 Resolver rules (when configured) before the control-plane switches routing.
- Adds a staged rollout hook to the installer: the installer will wait for all endpoints to be marked ready by the authenticator and for DNS priming to succeed for a configurable grace window.
- Includes Helm chart values for toggling staging behavior and for configuring priming timeouts.
- Adds e2e-like integration smoke tests (k8s job) that run in CI to exercise staging in a simulated multi-subnet layout.

Design notes and constraints:
- The authenticator runs in a best-effort reconciliation loop; it intentionally does not hold long-lived locks. It emits an annotated event stream (installer events) that the installer watches.
- DNS priming supports both Route53 private hosted zones and cross-account resolver rules; priming uses short-lived test records that are deleted on successful completion. There is a configurable priming TTL and retry budget.
- The staged hook defaults to OFF for existing customers to avoid behavioral surprises; the Helm value 'staging.enabled' toggles the behavior.

Backward compatibility and upgrade notes: 
- Feature is opt-in via Helm. No changes to the public control plane API.
- For customers who enable staging, upgrade time will increase by up to 'staging.maxGraceSeconds' while priming completes; documented in upgrade notes.
- Rollback plan: if priming fails and staging.failOpen=false, installer aborts and leaves previous endpoints intact. An operator can override with staging.failOpen=true to force cutover (documented).

Security considerations: 
- Priming worker only creates temporary test records and never exposes keys in logs. All actions are performed using the installer service principal and recorded in audit logs.
- The authenticator verifies SGs and IAM bindings; it does not change permissions automatically — it only flags mismatches and optionally populates a reconcile plan artifact that an operator can approve.

Notes for on-call: if operators see installer stalls during "staging:waiting_for_priming", check 'priming_success_total' metric and installer logs (installer/controllers/priming_worker.go). For quick recovery, operators can set staging.failOpen=true and re-run the installer to force cutover.
